announcements.text: A cron job whose run is interrupted by an OpenCrabs daemon restart delivers its result to NO channel: boot revival resumes the turn with no job identity, run id or deliver_to, so the job output reaches nobody. Ship-chain hot-reloads make restarts frequent, so any factory relying on cron delivery is exposed.

vpn/services/gatus/config/config.yaml carries live credentials in plaintext, including SSH private-key blocks. Never grep it with a context flag (-A/-B), and never print a parsed form of it - json.dumps of a single endpoint dict renders the key field verbatim. Read the KEY NAMES only; to compare a value, hash it in place. The read discipline is necessary but not sufficient: the PRINT is the second chokepoint, and it is the one that fails when the read felt safe. A third chokepoint is any TOOL whose output path renders the file's content: a diff, a checksum-and-dump, or a guard that prints a drift diff between two key-bearing copies discloses both. Read the output path before you ship the tool, not after.

announcements.text: infra_mac-cdp-tunnel (endpoint_id 15) was RED for 20 h 18 min: Gatus's own event table reads UNHEALTHY 2026-10-23T10:05:09Z -> HEALTHY 2026-10-24T06:23:09Z, and every probe in that window failed. An earlier version of this entry read '110 results / 0 failures', true only of the window it was read in, four hours before the outage began. THE MECHANISM, read from the endpoint's own definition rather than inferred: it is NOT a Mac-localhost check. The URL is ssh://78.17.187.4:15259 — which `getent hosts` resolves to THIS host, agents — and the body then runs `curl -s --max-time 3 http://localhost:9222/json/version | grep -c Macintosh` ON AGENTS. `grep -c` exits 1 on zero matches, so the probe is red whenever nothing listens on agents' loopback:9222; the probed object is the FORWARDER, not the Mac. THE MAC WAS HEALTHY THROUGHOUT: with the endpoint red, `ssh mac` succeeded and CDP answered Chrome/150.0.7871.1016 with a Macintosh User-Agent. THE DEFECT WAS SUPERVISION, NOW CLOSED AND PROVEN ACROSS A REBOOT. The forwarder was hand-launched every time, so it died and nothing brought it back. It is now a repo unit, agents/services/mac-cdp/mac-cdp-tunnel.service (vds-servers 6bd06c02), Restart=always with ServerAliveInterval 15 x3 — so ssh EXITS on a missed probe when the Mac sleeps instead of holding a half-open socket that reads up while forwarding nothing. Positive control, not assertion: the MainPID was killed deliberately, systemd restarted it (NRestarts 0 -> 1, listener back, predicate green). STRONGER EVIDENCE SINCE: the host itself was powered off at the hypervisor and rebooted on 2026-10-24 (boot 12:49), producing a SECOND red episode — UNHEALTHY 12:12:13Z -> HEALTHY 12:53:10Z, 41 min — and that one was the HOST, not the tunnel: the unit came back on boot (ActiveEnter 12:52:24, MainPID 730, NRestarts 0 because a boot start is not a crash-restart), both loopbacks bound, green since (103/103 results, newest 2026-10-25T18:23:09Z). So do not blame the tunnel for a red that the host's own poweroff explains — check `who -b` first. THE MONTH IS WORSE THAN ANY RETAINED WINDOW SHOWS: endpoint 15 is 7,700 successful of 43,045 executions = 82.11% failure, endpoint 13 (mac-tunnel) 3,273 of 8,614 = 62.00%, endpoint 21 (mac-backup) 14 of 28 = 50.00% — so 13 reading 106/106 today describes the last ~8.8 h, not the month. Anything longer than the retained window reads endpoint_uptimes.

announcements.text: THE HAZARD IS NO LONGER HYPOTHETICAL: the kernel OOM-killed this daemon at 2026-10-24T06:06:44Z. systemd's own record reads 'A process of this unit has been killed by the OOM killer' then 'Main process exited, code=killed, status=9/KILL', and dmesg carries oom-kill:constraint=CONSTRAINT_MEMCG with oom_memcg=/user.slice/user-0.slice/user@0.service/app.slice/opencrabs-ops.service, task=opencrabs, pid=3237387, oom_score_adj=100 — pid 3237387 being the very process the previous text called the live MainPID. The unit restarted at 06:06:50Z (MainPID 701185, NRestarts 4). NO FURTHER KILL SINCE: the user journal from 2026-10-24T00:00 to 2026-10-25T18:23Z carries that one kill and no other. Live at 2026-10-25T18:22:56Z, 14 minutes after a CLEAN stop/start at 18:08:43Z (journal reads 'Stopping' then 'Started', NRestarts 0 — a deliberate restart, not a kill), the incarnation is at memory.current 2,147,262,464 of 2,147,483,648 B = 99.99% (headroom 216 KiB), swap.current 756,682,752 of 2,684,354,560 = 28.19%, memory.peak 405,504 B OVER memory.max, memory.events high 0 / max 20,355 / oom 0 / oom_kill 0 — and that zero is the PER-INCARNATION counter: it reads 0 because the kill it should have counted happened to the PREVIOUS incarnation, so a fresh zero is not evidence of a clean life. THE WATCHER IS NOW PROVEN END TO END, which it was not when this entry was written: on that clean restart endpoint 34's own event table reads UNHEALTHY 2026-10-25T18:09:01Z -> HEALTHY 18:20:01Z, so the false-on-restart push fired and the 600 s heartbeat recovered it 11 min later. The same host also OOM-killed the FAMILY profile daemon (opencrabs.service, pid 4086328) at 2026-10-23T10:21:25Z, so this is a host-pressure pattern, not one unit's bad luck. THE RESERVE IS ONE REMAINDER, not the swap line — the kill predicate is current + swap.current >= max + swap.max, so headroom and swap-free are two distributions of a single number, sampled five times at 12 s intervals on 2026-10-23 reading 103 / 67 / 110 / 241 / 102 MiB; quote no single-instant burst/remainder ratio, because the same pair reads 2.47x, 4.87x or 15.9x depending only on which sample is chosen. Raising the cap is NOT a free option: Committed_AS exceeded CommitLimit by 439 MiB at the 2026-10-23T06:52:36Z read, and that gap itself moves fast, so carry the sign and not the magnitude. TWO MEASUREMENT TRAPS WILL MAKE THIS ENTRY LOOK FALSE. It describes a USER unit, so a bare `systemctl show opencrabs-ops.service` (system scope) answers MainPID=0, MemoryMax=infinity, ActiveState=inactive — fabricated defaults for a unit that does not exist at that scope; only `systemctl --user` answers, and it returns the cap. And `dmesg -T` reads 24 s AHEAD of the journal on this host (06:07:08 against 06:06:44 for the same kill) because it converts from monotonic with the current offset, so it is the wrong instrument for an instant. dmesg's ops-unit kill count is a RING-BUFFER WINDOW, not a lifetime total.

announcements.text: The two board/ledger agreement gates are RETIRED, not red. tests/test_close_board_recorded.py and tests/test_board_intake_recorded.py assert a board/ledger close agreement, and this factory's issue board IS its ledger — ONE surface — so the two-surface predicate is INAPPLICABLE rather than failed. They were declared RED BY DESIGN at ledger n=611 and were the only REDs in the 23-gate audit. As of 2026-10-19 they are retired through the KIT'S DECLARED-ABSENT STATE, never by deletion: each reads the declared boundary from docs/ledger-invariants.json, this tree declares none, so each prints a named SKIP ('no docs/ledger-invariants.json — the boundary is a DECLARED factory parameter (#78 clause b)') and STILL RUNS EVERY PROBE — 11 on the close gate, 15 on the intake gate. HOW TO READ THEM NOW: a SKIP is the expected, correct state and is NOT a regression; but a RED from either gate IS a real defect — the retire was built so it cannot disguise a removed or broken gate. The four judgement probes are hermetic (a synthetic tree), and each gate keeps a positive control: a DECLARED boundary must still fail a bad row. The old 'RED BY DESIGN, do not file as a regression' instruction is WITHDRAWN — filing one of these as a regression is now the wrong call only if it SKIPPED; if it FAILED, file it. Owner directive 2026-10-19: 'i don't want to be asked such low level questions any more' — q27 is answered and the class (kit convention, internal mechanics) is now HQ's to decide, never the owner register's. Commits aed7c5af (gates + roles/hq.md + ledger n=1482) and 0c4952eb (prose refs). Full audit after: 24/24 gates PASS.

announcements.text: The asymmetry this entry recorded has changed MECHANISM while holding in EFFECT, and the earlier mechanism is now false, so it is replaced rather than extended. On 2026-10-23T07:23Z `cpu.max` did not exist in opencrabs-ops.service's cgroup and cgroup.controllers read 'memory pids'. On 2026-10-25T18:22:56Z the controller IS delegated and `cpu.max` DOES exist: the unit's cgroup.controllers reads 'cpu memory pids', app.slice/cgroup.subtree_control reads 'cpu memory pids', app.slice carries CPUAccounting=yes and CPUQuotaPerSecUSec=infinity, and cpu.max reads 'max 100000'. WHAT IS STILL TRUE, and is the fact a peer needs: THERE IS NO CEILING IN EFFECT. 'max 100000' is an unlimited quota, and cpu.stat reads nr_periods 0 / nr_throttled 0 / throttled_usec 0 / nr_bursts 0, so the controller is present, accounted and idle — it throttles nothing. systemd's own stop line for the previous incarnation reads 'Consumed 5h 32min 14.340s CPU time', uncapped. WHAT I CANNOT ESTABLISH: the instant the delegation changed. I have a read showing it ABSENT at 2026-10-23T07:23Z and a read showing it PRESENT at 2026-10-25T18:22:56Z, and the host was powered off at the hypervisor and rebooted at 2026-10-24T12:49Z between them; I have no read inside that window, so the change is bounded to a 36 h interval and attributed to no act — do not record a cause I did not measure. THE LOAD FINDING STANDS and is why this entry exists: host-diag's calibration is a ldavg-15 series, and on 2026-10-23 load15 sat between its p99 8.63 and its 5-day max 12.99 with disk 87% and MemAvailable 1315 MB both inside their thresholds, so the load leg was the SOLE trigger — and the load is the factory's own concurrent gate runs, registry renders and test suites, not a host fault. Two 15 s and 20 s /proc/stat windows at 07:08:45Z-07:09:34Z read busy 98.38% / 99.01%, idle 1.62% / 0.99%. Steal is a DISTRIBUTION and not a single-instant property: 11.35% and 23.54% in adjacent windows against a 6.83% lifetime average, sar at the host's native 600 s reading 6.20% / 8.53% / 10.25%, so it rises and falls with our own load — a second cause alongside our work, never a substitute for it. THE RESERVE IS ONE REMAINDER: headroom plus swap-free sampled 103 / 67 / 110 / 241 / 102 MiB at 12 s intervals, so no single-instant burst/remainder ratio may be quoted — the same pair reads 4.4x to 15.9x depending only on the sample.
